node.label: FoldBot
node.summary: A home robot that folds laundry

node.label: Time-pressed professionals
node.summary: Parents who buy on time savings. Posts say a tool that saves a few hours a week is an instant buy and that price matters less when time is recovered.

node.label: Subscription-fatigued budget buyers
node.summary: Buyers who already pay for many subscriptions. Many object to $49/month, would accept a one-time price, and say they will stay with the incumbent if the price is above $49.

node.label: Incumbent-locked switchers
node.summary: Users whose data and workflows live in the market-leading incumbent. They want import and sync before switching and fear lock-in and data misuse.

node.label: Community-driven recommenders
node.summary: Buyers who adopt products when friends or group chats vouch for them. Peer switching stories and launch praise move them.

node.label: Reliability over features
node.summary: Buyers say a tool that crashes or is confidently wrong is worse than a simpler one. Incumbent crashes and errors come up repeatedly.

node.label: Subscription fatigue at $49/month
node.summary: Many prospects reject another recurring bill. They would pay once or stay with a cheaper or free option.

node.label: Lock-in and switching cost
node.summary: Prospects will not switch without import, sync, and export from the incumbent. Their existing data is the main barrier.

node.label: Data privacy and training on user content
node.summary: Buyers worry where uploaded data goes and whether it trains models. Some left the incumbent over a data policy change.

node.label: Long or complex onboarding
node.summary: Users abandon tools whose setup takes more than about five minutes. The incumbent's learning curve is a known complaint.

node.label: Skepticism toward AI hype and demos
node.summary: Many buyers distrust AI-powered claims and say demos break in real use. They ask whether the product is just a wrapper.

node.label: Mobile access and offline use
node.summary: Users do much of their work on phones and want offline support. The incumbent's mobile app is widely criticised.

node.label: Desire to reclaim time
node.summary: A recurring positive desire is to automate the chore and recover hours each week. This is the strongest reason to buy.

node.label: AI feature race and hype fatigue
node.summary: Product startups are adding AI features quickly, which raises buyer skepticism and makes AI claims less persuasive.

node.label: Backlash against the incumbent
node.summary: Price rises and data policy changes at the incumbent push some buyers to look for alternatives.

node.label: Rise of indie challengers
node.summary: Independent tools are gaining attention against the incumbent, creating room for a focused entrant.

node.label: Subscription fatigue among younger buyers
node.summary: Surveys and posts report that younger buyers are tiring of recurring app fees.

node.label: Big incumbent (unnamed market leader)
node.summary: The dominant product tool. It has broad features and a free tier but is criticised for crashes, confident errors, a weak mobile app, a steep learning curve, and data policy changes. Users have high switching costs.

node.label: Indie product tools
node.summary: Smaller tools are gaining attention as challengers to the incumbent, and buyers say the category is becoming more crowded.

node.label: Launch price $49/month
node.summary: The launch price is the main reference point. Many posts say it is steep, and some say they would try it only if it were under $49.

node.label: Preference for one-time payment
node.summary: Several buyers say they would pay once rather than subscribe. Stated WTP in the anchor interviews clusters around $36 for price-conscious users.

node.label: Low anchor from skeptical incumbent users
node.summary: Users locked into the incumbent state WTP near $25, and the incumbent's free tier sets a reference point.

node.label: Stated WTP for time savers
node.summary: Community recommenders and time-focused buyers state WTP near $57 when peers vouch or time savings are clear.
